record bytes -> data sync -> collision-safe hard-link publish -> temp unlink -> records-directory fsync

implementation.darwin_sync_policy: Attempt F_FULLFSYNC for file data, then fallback to fsync when F_FULLFSYNC is unavailable; receipt exposes the observed mode.
implementation.interrupted_temp_policy: Only .w53-pub-*.tmp regular non-symlink files within size bounds are tolerated, maximum 32 per directory; they are excluded from ledger record identity but never treated as committed evidence.
implementation.root_compatibility: W49/W50 record, head, checkpoint, handoff and W52 custody root payload formats are unchanged.

process_crash_protocol_stress.method: fork child, stop at selected durability boundary with _exit, reopen and run W50-shaped recovery

required_actions: capture observed F_FULLFSYNC vs fsync fallback mode
external process termination at every durability boundary
controlled reboot/power-loss cases where operationally safe
reopen ticket and accept only exact pre or exact post according to contract

limitations: NON_PARITY: W53 is ledger custody/durability hardening only.
Linux process termination and POSIX fsync stress do not prove iPhone/APFS power-loss behavior.
F_FULLFSYNC capability/success must be observed on the selected physical iPhone; fallback fsync is recorded rather than silently relabeled as full flush.
Directory creation above the caller-selected root is not made durable by W53 because W53 intentionally does not fsync outside the selected custody root.
Advisory writer serialization remains a cooperating-writer contract; external checkpoint/handoff/receipt roots remain the authority against out-of-protocol mutation or whole-directory rollback.
No rights-cleared real corpus, current-iPhone Moises reference/differential, physical audio/performance evidence or final HQ PARITY judgment is supplied by W53.
